state: Claim for the lake house, policy SEA-3309127. We closed the cottage up at the end of the season like we always do. We shut the water off at the main valve, but we didn't drain the lines this year because the plumber we usually use retired and we hadn't found a new one. The heat was set to 50 when we left, at least that's what we set it to. Our neighbor across the road, who keeps an eye on the place, called on Monday to say he saw water coming out under the back door. When we got up there on Tuesday the house was freezing inside, the thermostat display was blank, and a pipe under the kitchen sink had split. There was water through the kitchen and into the family room, the floors are buckled, and the lower cabinets are swollen. The electric company told us there was a neighborhood outage over the weekend during the cold snap, but power came back on Sunday afternoon. Our furnace is oil and the tank still has oil in it, so we don't know why it wouldn't have come back on. We haven't been up there since we closed it. We've owned the cottage for eleven years and never had a problem like this. The furnace was serviced in the spring. state: Remediation contractor report - Job 26-1188, 42 Fern Hollow Rd. Scope: Water loss from failed washing machine hose (second floor laundry), discovered by homeowner upon return from a two-day trip. Water migrated through the laundry subfloor into the ceiling of the dining room below and down the interior wall cavity to the finished basement. Moisture readings on arrival: laundry subfloor saturated; dining room ceiling drywall saturated, sagging in a 4x6 ft area; basement wall cavity elevated; basement carpet pad wet along one wall. Visible microbial growth observed on the back side of the dining room ceiling drywall (approx. 10 sq ft) and at the base of the basement wall cavity (approx. 6 sq ft). Actions: extracted standing water, removed and disposed of dining room ceiling drywall in affected area and 2 ft flood cut on basement wall, removed carpet pad, set 4 air movers and 2 dehumidifiers, applied antimicrobial. Recommend: post-remediation air sampling, replacement of laundry subfloor, re-drywall and paint dining ceiling and basement wall, carpet reinstallation with new pad. Homeowner states the hose was original to the machine, which is about nine years old. Photos: 46. Moisture logs attached. Homeowner's contents in basement (boxes of books, a futon) were wet along the same wall; homeowner has moved them to the garage. Equipment on site 5 days. Final moisture readings within dry standard on day 5 except laundry subfloor (still elevated; replacement recommended). Technician: R. Paz, IICRC WRT. state.claim: Water stain spreading on bedroom ceiling after last week's heavy rain. Roofer found cracked and curling shingles over that room and said the roof is at the end of its life. No storm damage like missing shingles or impact marks.
state.policy: Covers sudden and accidental direct physical loss. Excludes wear and tear, deterioration, and repeated seepage. Covers interior damage caused by rain only if the roof is first damaged by wind or hail.

criteria.definition: Deterioration without a wind or hail opening
Cause uncertain enough to need an independent inspection

interior_covered.note: Rain entered without prior wind or hail damage.
